misconceptions.description: Declaring readiness as a celebration that everything looks good rather than checking each prior artifact against a go or no-go criterion
misconceptions.trigger: review asserts readiness with no item-by-item check
misconceptions.feedback: Treat readiness as a gate that can fail. Check each prior artifact against a go or no-go criterion.

misconceptions.description: Running a readiness review that has no real failure condition, so a launch can never be blocked even when consent or policy is incomplete
misconceptions.trigger: review has no criterion that would stop a launch
misconceptions.feedback: Hold a no-go when a blocking item (such as unsent consent forms) is unmet. A gate must be able to fail.

misconceptions.description: Giving a readiness verdict with no reference to the specific section artifacts (tension map, transcript, rubric, policy memo, evidence plan) that justify it
misconceptions.trigger: verdict cites no prior artifact as the basis
misconceptions.feedback: Tie each go or no-go to the specific prior artifact that supports it so the verdict is auditable.

misconceptions.description: Accepting a plan to launch the AI tool now and gather consent or collect the baseline afterward, reversing the policy boundary
misconceptions.trigger: review approves launch before consent and baseline are in place
misconceptions.feedback: Do not launch before consent and baseline close. Reject plans that reverse the policy boundary.
